da-false-claim.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.md:11-16 claims a 'bijection between irreducible summands of V^{otimes n} under H_n(R,q) and knot/link types arising as closures of n-strand braids'.
da-false-claim.notes: The claimed bijection is not literally a bijection in the standard theory. Irreducible summands of V^{tensor n} for U_q(su2) are labelled by a small set (e.g. spins, ~ partitions with <=2 rows / n+1 summands by multiplicity), whereas knot/link types from n-strand braid closures are a vastly larger (infinite as n grows, and many braids close to the same knot via Markov moves) set. The Markov trace assigns a POLYNOMIAL (Jones) to a knot, it does not biject irreps with knot types. The map markovTraceMap : IrrepSummand n -> KnotType n being 'Bijective' (lean:43-44) is asserted as an axiom but is very likely FALSE as a literal bijection (cardinality mismatch). At minimum the statement conflates 'isotypic component' with 'knot type' without the matching equivalence. Warn (not hard fail) because the .lean axiomatises abstract opaque types so no concrete counterexample is forced, but the .md's natural reading is false.

da-vacuous.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.lean:26-30 declare IrrepSummand, KnotType, markovTraceMap as opaque 'axiom ... : Type' / opaque map, and :43 axiomatises Bijective(markovTraceMap n).
da-vacuous.notes: The Lean 'theorem knot_particle_correspondence' (line 46-50) is proved by direct appeal to the axiom knot_particle_correspondence_axiom - i.e. it ASSUMES exactly its conclusion. With IrrepSummand and KnotType being uninterpreted opaque types, the bijectivity axiom has no content (one can always axiomatise a bijection between two opaque Types of unspecified cardinality). The 'theorem' is a self-assuming projection of an axiom: it proves nothing beyond the axiom it cites. Honest as a recorded external result, but vacuous as a Lean theorem.

da-circular.notes: Not circular in the derivation sense - it does not assume a numerical target. (The Lean self-assumption is captured under da-vacuous / da-lean-narrative-divergence.)

da-overclaim.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.md:11 'establishing a bijection between: irreducible summands ... and knot/link types arising as closures of n-strand braids'.
da-overclaim.notes: 'Bijection' overclaims. The actual theorem (Jones 1987) is that the Markov trace defines a link INVARIANT (the Jones polynomial) via Hecke representations - a map FROM braid closures TO polynomials, factoring through trace functions, NOT a bijection between irreps and knot types. The proposition upgrades a trace/invariant construction to a bijection, which is a strictly stronger (and false) claim. The kind is 'proposition' (asserts a theorem), so the overclaim is load-bearing.

da-hidden-dof.notes: No hidden free parameter; V = V_{1/2} fundamental rep and H_n(R,q) are fixed inputs.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.md:11-13 'Then the Markov trace ... assigns to each irreducible summand a knot type K_lambda (the closure of any braid representative)'.
da-non-sequitur.notes: Gap: q-Schur-Weyl gives the decomposition of V^{tensor n} into irreps labelled by partitions (md:7-9, sound). But the step from 'irrep labelled by lambda' to 'a knot type K_lambda = closure of any braid representative' is a non-sequitur: a partition lambda labels an isotypic component, not a braid; there is no canonical braid 'representative' of an irrep whose closure yields a well-defined knot. The phrase 'the closure of any braid representative' presupposes a representative exists and that 'any' gives the same knot, neither of which is established. The Markov-trace-as-invariant connection is real but does not yield the asserted assignment irrep -> knot.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.lean:43-50 proves Function.Bijective(markovTraceMap n) over OPAQUE axiom-types by citing an axiom of the same statement; .md:1-21 asserts a concrete bijection with hadrons as 'tensor products of summands bound by Hopf links' (md:20-21).
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: Divergence on two counts: (i) the Lean proves a bijection between two uninterpreted opaque Types by ASSUMING it as an axiom - it does not formalise the q-Schur-Weyl / Markov-trace content the .md describes, so it is weaker/different (vacuously-axiomatised) than the narrative; (ii) the .md's hadron clause (md:19-21, 'hadrons correspond to tensor products of such summands bound by Hopf links') has no Lean counterpart at all. The .ts validation flag is 'not_checked'. proof-statement-integrity FAIL: the Lean does not derive the .md claim, it axiomatises a content-free shadow of it.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.lean:20-23,38-44 cite [jones1987] §3 (Markov trace) + §4 (link polynomials) as backing for the BIJECTION axiom.
da-citation-misuse.notes: Jones 1987 establishes the Markov trace -> link-polynomial invariant (Jones polynomial), NOT a bijection between Hecke irreducible summands and knot types. The citation supports the trace/invariant construction but is mis-attributed as backing for 'Function.Bijective(markovTraceMap)'. The reference is real and relevant to the area, but it does not contain the bijectivity claim it is cited to justify - hence citation-misuse (minor, since the paper IS the right source for the underlying machinery).

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.md:12 'a knot type K_lambda (the closure of any braid representative)'; md:1-2 mixes U_q(su(2)) rep V_{1/2} with H_n(R,q).
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: 'Knot type' vs 'link type' used interchangeably (md:13,16 say 'knot/link', md:12 says 'knot type K_lambda'); n-strand braid closures are generally LINKS not knots. 'The closure of any braid representative' - 'representative of what?' (an irrep is not a braid) and 'any' presumes well-definedness. Also the relation between the U_q(su2) R-matrix braiding picture and the H_n(R,q) Hecke picture is asserted via 'q-Schur-Weyl duality' without pinning which duality / which q-regime.

da-empirical-fragility.notes: No numerical/experimental match in this proposition; purely structural.

da-physical-implausibility.evidence: knot-particle-correspondence.md:19-21 'each localized knot (p,K) corresponds to a unique irreducible summand, and hadrons correspond to tensor products of such summands bound by Hopf links'.
da-physical-implausibility.notes: The physics mapping (knot <-> particle, hadron = Hopf-linked summands) is the framework's core ansatz, not independently testable here, but the 'unique irreducible summand' per localized knot inherits the bijection overclaim - if the underlying correspondence is not a bijection, 'unique' fails. A domain expert would note that real hadron quantum numbers (color SU(3), isospin) are not visibly recovered from 'tensor products bound by Hopf links'. Minor since it is framework-internal.

da-reproducibility.notes: No compute witness cited for this proposition; nothing to reproduce.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: major-revision. referee_argument: The strongest objection is that the headline claim - a BIJECTION between Hecke irreducible summands and knot/link types from braid closures - is an overstatement of the genuine Jones-1987 result (Markov trace gives a link INVARIANT / Jones polynomial, a many-to-one trace map, not a bijection; cardinalities do not match). The Lean compounds this by 'proving' Function.Bijective over opaque uninterpreted Types via an axiom that simply ASSUMES the conclusion (self-assuming projection), and omits the hadron clause entirely - a proof-statement-integrity failure. Fix: restate the proposition as 'the Markov trace defines a link invariant assigning each braid closure its Jones polynomial, and each localized knot a well-defined isotypic weight' (the true claim), drop 'bijection', and either formalise the q-Schur-Weyl decomposition honestly or downgrade the Lean to a cited-axiom remark. The [jones1987] citation should be re-scoped to the invariant construction it actually supports.
